bullets.text: ML is a subfield of Artificial Intelligence (AI).
Systems learn patterns from data rather than fixed rules.
Models improve over time with more data without reprogramming.
Teaches computers to learn from experience, like humans.
ML is ubiquitous: Netflix recommendations, spam filters, virtual assistants.
Growth driven by vast data availability.
Enhanced computational power (GPUs) for data processing.
Development of sophisticated algorithms.

sections.heading: Three Main Types of Machine Learning

bullets.text: Supervised Learning: learns from labeled data.
Unsupervised Learning: discovers patterns in unlabeled data.
Reinforcement Learning: learns through interaction and feedback.
Most common type, uses datasets with inputs and correct outputs.
Model learns relationships to predict outputs for new inputs.
Example: predicting house prices based on features and sale prices.
Categories: Regression (continuous values) and Classification (discrete labels).
Works with unlabeled data to find inherent patterns or structures.
Application: Clustering, like grouping customers by buying behavior.
Application: Dimensionality reduction to simplify complex datasets.
An agent learns by interacting with an environment.
Receives rewards or penalties to adjust its strategy.
Goal: learn a policy to maximize total reward over time.
Examples: training robots, game-playing AI (AlphaGo), self-driving cars.
Data quality: noisy, biased, or incomplete data impacts performance.
Overfitting: model learns training data too well, fails on new data.
Ethical concerns: biased data can lead to biased models with real-world consequences.
Recap of ML definition, importance, types, and challenges.
Future lectures will explore algorithms and practical applications.
